stem: The Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was INSTITUTED in:
explanation: Bharat Ratna instituted on 2 January 1954 by President Rajendra Prasad. First three recipients (1954) — Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari, C.V. Raman. Suspended once during 1977-80 (Janata Party era). Awarded for 'exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour' — initially restricted to arts/literature/science/public service; expanded in 2011 to ANY field. Maximum 3 awards in a year (norm; 2024 was an exception). No formal title — recipients can describe themselves as 'Awarded Bharat Ratna by the President of India'.
subject: General Knowledge

stem: Among the FIRST batch of Bharat Ratna recipients in 1954 was the Nobel laureate physicist:

options.option_text: C.V. Raman (Nobel 1930, for the Raman effect)

explanation: 1954 first three: C. Rajagopalachari (last GG of India), Dr S. Radhakrishnan (philosopher, 2nd President), C.V. Raman (Nobel 1930 for the Raman scattering effect). Other Nobel laureates honoured with the Bharat Ratna: Mother Teresa (Nobel Peace 1979 → Bharat Ratna 1980); Amartya Sen (Nobel Economics 1998 → Bharat Ratna 1999). Homi Bhabha (founder of Indian nuclear programme) and S. Chandrasekhar (Nobel 1983 — the Chandrasekhar limit) were NOT awarded the Bharat Ratna. APJ Abdul Kalam received it in 1997.

stem: How many Bharat Ratnas were announced in 2024 — the largest number in a single year since the award's institution?

options.option_text: 5 (Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, Chaudhary Charan Singh, P.V. Narasimha Rao, M.S. Swaminathan)

explanation: 5 Bharat Ratnas announced in 2024 (an unprecedented count — earlier max in a year was 3): (1) Karpoori Thakur — former Bihar CM, socialist, posthumous (announced 23 Jan 2024, his birth centenary); (2) Lal Krishna Advani — BJP veteran, ex-Deputy PM (only living recipient of the 2024 batch); (3) Chaudhary Charan Singh — former PM, kisan-leader, posthumous; (4) P.V. Narasimha Rao — former PM, architect of 1991 reforms, posthumous; (5) M.S. Swaminathan — Father of India's Green Revolution, posthumous. The latter three were announced together on 9 February 2024.

stem: Karpoori Thakur, awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 (on his birth centenary), was a former Chief Minister of:
explanation: Karpoori Thakur (1924-1988) — 'Jan Nayak'. Bihar CM twice — 1970-71 (Socialist) and 1977-79 (Janata Party). Pioneered Mungeri Lal Commission-based reservation for OBCs in Bihar (1978) — backbone of Mandal politics later. Born in a Nai (barber) caste family, became a champion of the EBC (Extremely Backward Classes). Award announced 23-Jan-2024 on his birth centenary. The award was widely seen as politically symbolic given OBC focus in 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
subject: General Knowledge

stem: Which agriculture scientist, known as the 'Father of India's Green Revolution', received the Bharat Ratna POSTHUMOUSLY in 2024?
explanation: M.S. Swaminathan (Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan, 1925-2023) — agricultural scientist; led the introduction of high-yielding wheat varieties + Mexican dwarf wheat in collaboration with Norman Borlaug (1960s). Headed the National Commission on Farmers (2004-06) — 'Swaminathan Commission' — recommended MSP at C2+50%. Received many awards: Padma Shri/Bhushan/Vibhushan, World Food Prize 1987, and finally Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024. Norman Borlaug — American agronomist, Nobel Peace 1970, NOT Indian (so not eligible for Bharat Ratna). Verghese Kurien — 'Father of White Revolution' / Operation Flood (Amul); has not been awarded the Bharat Ratna.

stem: Which two NON-INDIANS have been awarded the Bharat Ratna?

options.option_text: Aung San Suu Kyi and Dalai Lama
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987) and Nelson Mandela (1990)

explanation: Two non-Indian Bharat Ratna recipients: (1) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987) — 'Frontier Gandhi' / 'Bacha Khan', Pakistani Pashtun nationalist; first non-Indian recipient. (2) Nelson Mandela (1990) — South African anti-apartheid leader, later President. Both honoured for non-violent struggle. Mother Teresa (1980) was awarded — she had taken Indian citizenship in 1948, so not technically a non-Indian recipient. Annie Besant — pre-independence (1933 death), so never awarded. Subhash Chandra Bose — was awarded posthumously in 1992 but withdrawn after a PIL questioning the proof of his death.
subject: General Knowledge

stem: Which former Prime Minister, who served briefly during 1979-80 and was a champion of the kisan / farmer cause, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024?
explanation: Chaudhary Charan Singh (1902-1987) — 5th PM of India (Jul 1979-Jan 1980, ~6 months, briefest tenure besides Gulzarilal Nanda's interim role). Founder of Bharatiya Lok Dal; champion of the agrarian middle / OBC peasants. Architect of the Zamindari Abolition Act in UP (1952). His birth anniversary (23 Dec) is celebrated as 'Kisan Diwas'. Awarded Bharat Ratna posthumously on 9 Feb 2024 (alongside Narasimha Rao and Swaminathan). Morarji Desai — Bharat Ratna 1991. V.P. Singh and I.K. Gujral — never awarded.

stem: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour. When was it first awarded?
subject: GK
explanation: Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954; the first three recipients were Dr. C.V. Raman, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

stem: Who was the first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna?
subject: GK
explanation: Indira Gandhi received the Bharat Ratna in 1971 — the first woman to receive it.

stem: The Bharat Ratna was awarded posthumously to Subhash Chandra Bose in 1992. Why was it revoked?

options.option_text: A Supreme Court ruling found posthumous awards invalid at the time

subject: GK
explanation: The Supreme Court (1997) held that at the time, the governing rules did not explicitly permit posthumous awards; the 1992 award to Bose was revoked.

stem: Sachin Tendulkar received the Bharat Ratna in which year, becoming the youngest recipient and the first sportsperson?
subject: GK
explanation: Sachin Tendulkar was awarded Bharat Ratna in 2013 (announced Nov 2013) — youngest ever at 40, and first sportsperson.

stem: C.N.R. Rao (scientist) and who else jointly received the Bharat Ratna in 2013–14?
subject: GK
explanation: Both C.N.R. Rao (materials scientist) and Sachin Tendulkar received Bharat Ratna in the same cycle (2013–14).

stem: Madan Mohan Malaviya received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2015. He was best known as:

options.option_text: Freedom fighter and founder of BHU

subject: GK
explanation: Madan Mohan Malaviya (1861–1946) founded Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916 and was a prominent moderate Congress leader.

stem: Atal Bihari Vajpayee (former PM) received the Bharat Ratna in which year?
subject: GK
explanation: Vajpayee received Bharat Ratna in 2015 (along with Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, posthumously).

stem: In 2024, four Bharat Ratnas were announced. Which of the following was one of the recipients?
subject: GK
explanation: 2024 Bharat Ratna recipients included Karpoori Thakur (posthumous), LK Advani, PV Narasimha Rao (posthumous), and MS Swaminathan (posthumous).

stem: MS Swaminathan, awarded Bharat Ratna in 2024, is known for his contribution to:
subject: GK
explanation: M.S. Swaminathan is the 'Father of India's Green Revolution' for introducing high-yielding wheat varieties in the 1960s.

stem: How many individuals have received the Bharat Ratna more than once?
subject: GK
explanation: Rajendra Prasad is the only person to have received Bharat Ratna twice (1962 and as President). Most sources say he received it once in 1962.

stem: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in which year?
subject: GK
explanation: Ambedkar received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990, during V.P. Singh's government.

stem: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani classical vocalist, received the Bharat Ratna in which year?
subject: GK
explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi received Bharat Ratna in 2009; known for the Kirana gharana of Hindustani classical music.

stem: Which Bharat Ratna recipient was a noted classical musician who performed the 'Vande Mataram' at the UN General Assembly?
subject: GK
explanation: M.S. Subbulakshmi (Carnatic vocalist, Bharat Ratna 1998) gave a memorable concert at the UN General Assembly in 1966.

stem: L.K. Advani, who received the Bharat Ratna in 2024, is associated with which political party?
subject: GK
explanation: L.K. Advani is a founding member of the BJP and former Deputy Prime Minister of India.

stem: The Bharat Ratna is given in the field of:

subject: GK
explanation: Bharat Ratna can be awarded for exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field — arts, literature, science, sports, public service.

stem: APJ Abdul Kalam, missile scientist and President, received the Bharat Ratna in:
subject: GK
explanation: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam received Bharat Ratna in 1997 while serving as Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government.

stem: Which year saw the largest number of Bharat Ratna awards in a single year — 6 awardees?
subject: GK
explanation: 1999 was the year with 6 recipients: Amartya Sen, Gopinath Bordoloi (posthumous), Ravi Shankar, Bismillah Khan, MS Subbulakshmi (1998 ceremony); 1999 included Jayaprakash Narayan (posthumous) and others.
